lawyer:
Md Arshad Ullah, Advocate-----For the Petitioner: 
Md Imam Hasan. Advocate------For the Respondent No.2.
parties:
Afifa Sultana ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Judge, Artha Rin Adalat and others -----Respondents
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : In this rule nisi the petitioner called in question the legality of the judgment and decree dated 17-2-2004 (decree signed on 23-2- 2004, Annexure-D and E to the writ petition respectively) passed by the learned Judge of the Arrha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Altha Rin Suit No. 371 of 2003. The petitioner also challenged the initiation of the proceeding of Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 without drawing up final decree as well as Order No.4 dated 29-11-2007 for issuance of sale proclamation without passing order of sale as required under Order XXI, rule 64 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the successive orders passed in the execution case. 

 3. The Bank fraudulently by giving false address of the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 2003 (renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 371 of 2003) and the summon of the suit was not served upon the petitioner. Therefore, the petitioner was not aware about the institution of the suit. However, the suit was decreed on contest against the Company  and other defendants and ex parte against the defendant-petitioner by judgment and decree dated 17-2-2004 (decree signed on 23-2-2004). The Bank there- after filed Artha Jari Case No. 214 Of 2007 on the basis of the preliminary decree signed on 23-2-2004 before the Adalat prior to drawing up of the final decree and the learned Judge of the Adalat directed to publish the auction sale notice by order dated 29- 11-2007 in the daily newspaper under section 33(1) of the Ain but no one participated in the auction. Eventually, on an application filed by the Bank for issuance of title under section 33(7) of the Ain, the learned Judge of the Adalat issued certificate of title by order dated 25-6-2009. The petitioner came to know about the suit and the proceeding of the execution case in the first week of March, 2010 from respondent No.3 (brother of the petitioner) and filed this writ petition. 

 6. The Bank filed an affidavit-in-reply that on prayer of the Company, the Bank, as a financial institution allowed term loan, cash credit (hypo), cash credit (pledge), L/C limit in favour of the Company. The petitioner is a director of the said Messrs Romana Industries Limited (the Company) and as security for repayment of the said loan; the petitioner mortgaged her property by executing registered deed of mortgage and power of attorney in favour of the Bank. The petitioner also created further charge for rest amount of the loan liabilities of the Company and created equitable mortgage by depositing relevant documents of her title with the Bank and signed and executed memorandum of deposit of Title Deeds. The Bank filed Title Suit No. 45 of 2003 before the Adalat against Messrs Romana Industries Limited and its directors for recovery of outstanding loan liabilities. Three addresses of the petitioner were mentioned in the cause title of the plaint, one is 16/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Satrowja, Police Station-Kotwali, Dhaka which is the registered address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited, another address is 171, Bhagalpur, Savar, Dhaka which is factory address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited and last one is 20/1, Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka which has been given in the Memorandum and Articles of Association of Messrs Romana Industries Limited by the petitioner as her address. The summons of the Artha Rin Suit was duly served upon the defendants of Artha Rin Suit and three defendants including the Company, its Managing Director and others appeared in the suit. The suit was decreed on contest against the said defendants by judgment and decree dated 17-2-2004 (decree signed on 23-2-2004). After completion of all legal formalities the Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 331 of 2004. Eventually, a certificate was issued in favour of the Bank under section 33(5) of the Ain. Subsequently, the Bank filed a second execution case being Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 on 21-7-2009 and in the second execution case on prayer of the Bank certificate of title was issued in its favour under section 33(7) of the Ain which has already been registered with the office of sub-registrar. Narayangonj. The summons and the notices were duly served upon the petitioner in accordance with law and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 7. Mr Md Asadullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that on perusal of the plaint it is evident that the residential address of the defendant-petitioner was not given in the plaint of the suit as required under Order VII, rule 1(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code. in short), He next submits that the Bank intentionally avoided to mention the residential address of the petitioner which has been given in the deed of mortgage as well as in the power of attorney and the Bank obtained the Judgment and decree by fraudulent means. He further submits that the execution case filed after the preliminary decree and before the final decree illegally and therefore the execution proceeding is liable to be struck down. He next submits that direction for publishing auction sale notice of the mortgage property without passing any order of sale as required under Order XXI, rule 64 of the Code is illegal and it is liable to be struck down. He lastly submits that the petitioner is liable to pay Taka 20,000 with interest as per the terms of mortgage deed and she is willing to pay the same to save her property and necessary order may be passed accordingly. 

 8. In reply. Mr Md Imam Hasan, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2 Bank has taken us through the plaint of the suit, deed of mortgage. power of attorney as well as the Memorandum and Articles of Association of Messrs Romana Industries Limited (shortly, the Memorandum) and contends that in the plaint three addresses of the petitioner were given and all those are correct addresses of the defendant-petitioner. He next con- tends that in the deed of mortgage number of holding was mentioned but in the power of attorney the number of holding was not given by the petitioner and therefore, to avoid confusion the Bank used the address of the petitioner as was given by her in the Memorandum of the Company. He further contends that the allegations that the Bank obtained decree by committing fraud upon the Adalat by using false address is not true and all the addresses given by the Bank in the plaint are correct addresses of the petitioner. He also contends that it has already been settled in a good number of cases by this Division that in an Artha Rin Suit an execution case may be filed after preliminary decree and after selling of the mortgage property the preliminary decree shall be made final. He next contends that writ petition against judgment and decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat is not maintainable as alternative forum of appeal is available under section 41 of the Ain. He further contends that admittedly two full brothers of the petitioner contested the suit and so, it is hardly believable that the petitioner was not aware about the suit and execution cases. He lastly contends that the proceeding of the Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 is lawful and the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 17. In this case, the Bank used three correct addresses of the petitioner and the petitioner herself used her address as 20/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka in the Memorandum. It is true that the Bank could have also used the address of the petitioner which has been stated in the deed of mortgage as well as the power of attorney. But in the power of attorney holding number is absent in the place of address. We have already seen that the Bank used three addresses of the petitioner and, as such, we find no substance in the allegations that the Bank used false address of the petitioner in the plaint and obtained judgment and decree by fraudulent means. Rather, the petitioner made untrue statements in paragraph 7 of the writ petition about use of false address and has not come with clean hands to avail equitable relief in writ jurisdiction. Moreover, in writ jurisdiction it cannot be ascertained whether summons were duly upon the petitioner or not as the Bank claims that summons were served upon the petitioner. The question whether 20/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka is the residential address of the petitioner or whether 18, lshdhair Road, Fatullah, Narayangonj is the residential address of the petitioner or whether the petitioner is Hable for Taka 20,000 with interest are all disputed questions of facts which cannot be decided in the writ jurisdiction without proper evidence. 

 18. It has been decided in the cases of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank LId reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, Gazi M Towfiq vs Agrani Bank, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation vs Artha Rin Adalat, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6 and Edruk Limited vs Secretary. Ministry of Industries, reported in 14 BLC 102 and in a good number of cases by the Appellate Division as well as High Court Division that a writ petition is not maintainable against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat as alternative forum of appeal is available under section 41 of the Ain. 

 19. By now it is a settled principle of law that a judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged in writ jurisdiction except coramnon-judice or fraud committed upon Adalat in obtaining the judgment and the decree. 

 20. In this case it is not disputed that the learned Judge of the Adalat had lawful jurisdiction to pass the impugned judgment and decree. The question as to whether the judgment and decree has been obtained by practicing fraud upon the Adalat is a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. Moreover, the petitioner failed to prove any apparent fraud committed by the Bank in obtaining the judgment and decree. Therefore challenging of the judgment and decree in writ jurisdiction is not maintainable. 

 21. The next question is whether the execution case may be tiled after preliminary decree. 

 22. It has been decided by this Division by judgment dated 29-8-2007 passed in Writ Petition No. 3672 of 2004 in consideration of the provisions of section 5(3)(4) of the Ain that in a suit for recovery of loan by sell of mortgage property, the decree shall be deemed to be a final decree only when the property mortgaged in favour of the plaintiff is sold in auction in accordance with the decree and filing of an execution case after the preliminary decree is lawful. 

 23. Thus, we find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that filing of the execution case after preliminary decree is unlawful.
